article.title: Common mistake: 'discuss about' vs 'discuss'
article.description: Wrong: 'Let's discuss about the plan.' Right: 'Let's discuss the plan.' Teaching point: 'discuss' is a transitive verb that already means 'talk about' — adding 'about' after it is redundant, though very common among learners.
article.content: Wrong: 'Let's discuss about the plan.' Right: 'Let's discuss the plan.' Teaching point: 'discuss' is a transitive verb that already means 'talk about' — adding 'about' after it is redundant, though very common among learners.

generated.caption:
Ever said "Let's discuss about the plan" and gotten a strange look? 🤔 Here's a quick fix!

The verb 'discuss' already means 'talk about', so adding 'about' is redundant. You just need 'discuss'! For example, say 'Let's discuss the plan,' not 'Let's discuss about the plan.' It's a common mistake that will make your English sound more natural!

Save this simple tip & follow @EnglishVault for more daily English lessons!

slides.body: It's a common mistake many English learners make, but the phrase 'discuss about' is actually redundant. The verb 'discuss' is transitive, meaning it already carries the sense of 'talking about' a particular subject. Therefore, adding 'about' after it creates an unnecessary repetition. For example, instead of saying, 'Let's discuss about the plan,' the correct and more concise way is simply, 'Let's discuss the plan.' Remember, just like you wouldn't say 'enter into the room' (you just 'enter the room'), 'discuss' doesn't need an 'about'.
